corrections.why: Both lookout pages say the tower was removed in 1999 and moved to a museum in Pierce. The index's 'Gone' does not record the move.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1947 Clearwater association annual report gives 1931 for the first tower; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts start the timeline in 1933 with a 100-foot pole tower. The story gives both dates and does not choose.
The annual report says the 1947 steel towers were 75 feet and replaced two wooden lookouts; two lookout pages give an 86-foot Army surplus steel tower built in 1948. Both are reported.
The index says Gone, which is accurate for the original site. The lookout pages say the tower moved to Pierce in 1999. The story follows the pages.

Firelookout.com says 'the tower' was removed in 1999 right after the 1948 steel tower entry; Forest Lookouts says only that a tower was moved to Pierce, with no date. The story says the entries suggest the 1948 steel tower.
Lookout pages name the Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association; the 1947 report names the Clearwater TPA. The story does not name the agency.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' is corrected to 'relocated': two lookout pages say the tower moved to Pierce in 1999. Not verified: whether the moved tower is on display. The Pierce museum is named only as 'the Pierce museum' in the lookout pages; the Bradbury museum is named in a Pierce visitor guide, and the link between them is unconfirmed. Two search-result items (a Clearwater Tribune museum article and a Ray Coon obituary that mentions the lookout) could not be fetched (HTTP 429 and 403) and are not used. Planned WebSearch count: two used. Photos: lookout pages credit the Fire Lookout Museum but give no image URLs, so none recorded.
